date.as_written: vāravyomograviṣvagvadanaparimite lakṣmaṇakṣoṇipālapravyaktābde valakṣe tava hara sutithau drāk tapasyasya rātrau

purpose: for the merit of the scribe (pāpahaṃ lekhakasya); the closing saṅkalpa is a formula for hearing the Rāmāyaṇa
notes: The era is the Lakṣmaṇasena era (lakṣmaṇakṣoṇipālapravyaktābde). Reading the chronogram from the right: vāra = 7 (units), vyoman = 0 (tens), ugra = Rudra = 11?, viṣvagvadana ('faces on all sides' = Brahmā) = 4?. A Rudra value of 11 does not give a plausible year. If ugra stands for a single digit, the year would be about LS 4x07 or x07; a value around LS 407 (≈1526 CE) would fit the usual range of LS dates, but this is conjectural, so ce_approx is left empty. The date falls on the śukla tithi sacred to Hara in Phālguna, at night. The scribe does not give his name; he describes himself as having his head at Rāma's lotus-feet ('udyatsvakarppo' is corrupt and may conceal a name or epithet). 'dhanapatiramaṇaṃ' qualifies the copied ādikāṇḍa as 'delighting Dhanapati' (a common Maithil name, possibly the patron), but it could also be a pun on Kubera; the person reading is low-confidence. The closing 'oṃ sakala… vālmīkikṛtarāmāyaṇaśravaṇam ahaṅ kariṣye' is a standard saṅkalpa for hearing the Rāmāyaṇa ('dyādi' is probably for 'adyādi'). It does not record who commissioned or owned this copy.
